senses.def: used before a singular noun when you mention it for the first time or it is not specific
senses.ar: (أداة نكرة تسبق الاسم المفرد، تُترجم غالباً بالتنوين)
ex: I have a brother and a sister.
She wants a new phone.

senses.def: used to say how much or how often for each one of something
ex: The tickets cost five pounds a person.

mistake.wrong: She is teacher.
mistake.right: She is a teacher.
mistake.note: English needs a/an before a singular job noun, but Arabic does not use an article here.

senses.def: something that has both good and bad effects
ex: Fame can be a double-edged sword.
Online anonymity is a double-edged sword: it protects activists but also trolls.

mistake.wrong: It's a sword with two edges.
mistake.right: It's a double-edged sword.
mistake.note: Idioms are fixed. Translating سلاح ذو حدين word for word breaks the idiom.

senses.def: a matter about which people disagree, or one that is no longer important
senses.ar: مسألة خلافية؛ أمر لم يَعُد مهماً
ex: Whether he knew is a moot point now.
It's a moot point whether the plan would have worked.

mistake.wrong: It's a mute point.
mistake.right: It's a moot point.
mistake.note: moot /muːt/ and mute /mjuːt/ sound different and mean different things.

senses.def: to leave someone or something and not come back for them
ex: They had to abandon the car in the snow.
He abandoned his family when the children were small.

senses.def: to stop doing a plan or activity before it is finished
ex: The match was abandoned because of rain.
The company abandoned its plan to build a new factory.

mistake.wrong: He abandoned from his family.
mistake.right: He abandoned his family.
mistake.note: abandon takes a direct object, with no preposition.

senses.def: left by the people who owned or used it and no longer cared for
ex: We found an abandoned house at the end of the road.
Abandoned cars were left along the motorway.

senses.def: something that is different from what is normal or expected, often in a bad way
ex: His rude reply was an aberration; he is usually very polite.
Scientists studied the aberration in the data.

senses.def: to hate something very much, especially for moral reasons
ex: She abhors cruelty to animals.
Many people abhor violence of any kind.

senses.def: so bad that it makes people feel strong disgust or anger
ex: Slavery is abhorrent to most people today.
He found the idea of lying to her abhorrent.

senses.def: the physical or mental power that lets you do something
ex: She has the ability to speak four languages.
His ability to stay calm is impressive.

senses.def: a natural skill or talent
ex: Students of all abilities are welcome in the class.

senses.def: extremely bad, especially a sad or hopeless situation
ex: Many families live in abject poverty.
The team's abject failure shocked the fans.

senses.def: having the power, skill or chance to do something
ex: Will you be able to come on Friday?
She was able to finish the work early.

senses.def: good at doing things; clever and skilled
ex: He is an able teacher who is loved by his pupils.

mistake.wrong: I will can help you tomorrow.
mistake.right: I will be able to help you tomorrow.
mistake.note: can has no future form, so use will be able to.

senses.def: different from what is usual, often in a way that is worrying
ex: The doctor found an abnormal heartbeat.
It is abnormal for the weather to be this cold in July.

senses.def: on or onto a ship, plane, train or bus
ex: The plane is ready, so please come aboard.
All aboard! The train is leaving.

senses.def: on or onto a ship, plane, train or bus
ex: There were two hundred passengers aboard the ship.
We went aboard the ferry at noon.

senses.def: a little more or less than a number or amount
ex: It costs about ten pounds.
She left at about six o'clock.

senses.def: on the subject of; concerning
ex: We talked about the film.
This book is about a young soldier.

senses.def: in or to different parts of a place
ex: Toys were lying about the room.

mistake.wrong: We discussed about the problem.
mistake.right: We discussed the problem.
mistake.note: discuss is followed directly by its object; do not add about, although talk about is correct.

senses.def: a time when someone is not at a place where they should be
ex: Her absence from school lasted two weeks.
In his absence, Sam ran the meeting.

senses.def: the fact that something does not exist or is not there
ex: The absence of clear rules caused confusion.

senses.def: not at a place where you should be, for example at school or work
ex: Three students were absent today.
He was absent from work with a cold.

mistake.wrong: He was absent in the lesson.
mistake.right: He was absent from the lesson.
mistake.note: Use absent from, not absent in or at.

senses.def: complete and total, used to give emphasis
ex: I have absolute trust in my doctor.
That film was an absolute disaster.

senses.def: not limited or controlled by anyone or anything
ex: The king had absolute power over the country.

senses.def: a rule or principle that is always true, whatever the situation
ex: She does not believe in moral absolutes.
In science, few things are absolutes.

senses.def: completely; used to give strong emphasis
ex: You are absolutely right.
The food was absolutely delicious.

senses.def: used as a strong way of saying yes or agreeing
ex: 'Do you agree?' 'Absolutely!'

mistake.wrong: The film was absolutely good.
mistake.right: The film was absolutely brilliant.
mistake.note: absolutely goes with strong words like brilliant, terrible or amazing, not plain good or bad.

senses.def: so silly or unreasonable that it is difficult to take seriously
ex: It is absurd to pay so much for a plain shirt.
The idea sounded absurd at first, but it worked.

senses.def: in very large amounts; used to emphasise how clear something is
ex: It was abundantly clear that she was unhappy.
Wild flowers grow abundantly in these hills.

senses.def: cruel or violent treatment of a person or animal
ex: The charity helps children who have suffered abuse.
Reports of abuse in the home must be taken seriously.

senses.def: the use of something in a bad or harmful way
ex: Drug abuse is a serious problem for many cities.
The abuse of power by officials angered voters.

senses.def: relating to schools, colleges or universities, and to studying
ex: The academic year starts in September.
She has good academic results.

senses.def: of interest in theory only and of no practical importance
ex: The question is academic now, because the shop has closed.

senses.def: a school or college that teaches a particular subject or skill
ex: He studied music at a famous academy in Vienna.
She joined the police academy last year.

senses.def: a way of pronouncing words that shows where a person is from
ex: He has a strong Scottish accent.
Her English accent is easy to understand.

senses.def: a mark above a letter or the stress on part of a word
ex: The accent in the word 'banana' falls on the second syllable.

senses.def: to take something that someone offers you
ex: She accepted the gift with a smile.
Do you accept credit cards?

senses.def: to agree that something is true or right, or to say yes to an offer
ex: He accepted the job last week.
We must accept that we made a mistake.

mistake.wrong: I accepted to help them.
mistake.right: I agreed to help them.
mistake.note: accept takes a noun or that-clause, not to + verb; use agree to + verb.

senses.def: a way of entering a place or of reaching something
ex: The only access to the village is by boat.
Students have free access to the library.

senses.def: the right or chance to use or see something
ex: Many homes in the area have no access to clean water.

senses.def: to find, open or get information on a computer
ex: You can access your account from any device.
Only staff can access these files.

mistake.wrong: She has an access to the internet.
mistake.right: She has access to the internet.
mistake.note: access is uncountable, so do not use a/an with it.

senses.def: a bad event that happens without being planned, in which someone may be hurt
ex: He had a car accident on Monday.
Nobody was hurt in the accident.

senses.def: something that happens by chance, without being planned
ex: We met by accident at the station.

senses.def: happening by chance and not on purpose
ex: The fire was accidental.
It was an accidental discovery.

senses.def: by chance or by mistake, not on purpose
ex: I accidentally deleted the photo.
She accidentally left her keys at home.

senses.def: a place where you can live or stay, such as a room or hotel
ex: The price includes accommodation and breakfast.
Students often look for cheap accommodation near the university.

mistake.wrong: We need an accommodation for two nights.
mistake.right: We need accommodation for two nights.
mistake.note: accommodation is uncountable in British English, so it has no a/an and no plural.

senses.def: to go somewhere with someone
ex: A nurse accompanied the patient to the hospital.
Children must be accompanied by an adult.

senses.def: to happen or exist at the same time as something else
ex: A cough often accompanies a high temperature.

senses.def: to play music while someone sings or plays another instrument
ex: She accompanied the singer on the piano.

senses.def: to succeed in doing something difficult or planned
ex: We accomplished everything we planned.
What do you hope to accomplish this year?

senses.def: in a way that fits the situation
ex: The rules have changed, so please act accordingly.
He was told the facts and replied accordingly.

senses.def: for that reason; as a result
ex: The road was closed. Accordingly, we took another route.

senses.def: an arrangement with a bank to keep your money there
ex: I opened a bank account last week.
She checked her account online.

senses.def: a record of a person who uses a website or service
ex: You need an email account to join.

senses.def: a spoken or written description of an event
ex: He gave a clear account of what happened.

senses.def: to explain the reason for something (account for)
ex: How do you account for the sudden drop in sales?

senses.def: to form a particular part of a total (account for)
ex: Tourism accounts for ten per cent of the country's income.

senses.def: the fact of being responsible for your actions and having to explain them
ex: The public wants more accountability from politicians.
Clear rules give the team a sense of accountability.

senses.def: a person whose job is to keep or check the money records of a person or company
ex: My accountant helps me with my tax forms.
She works as an accountant for a large firm.

senses.def: correct and exact, with no mistakes
ex: Make sure the information is accurate.
He gave an accurate description of the thief.

senses.def: a statement that someone has done something wrong or illegal
ex: He denied the accusation of stealing.
The accusations against her were false.

senses.def: to say that someone has done something wrong or illegal
ex: She accused him of lying.
The man was accused of stealing a car.

mistake.wrong: They accused him for stealing.
mistake.right: They accused him of stealing.
mistake.note: Use accuse someone of something, not for.

senses.def: familiar with something because you have often experienced it
ex: She is accustomed to getting up early.
We soon grew accustomed to the noise.

senses.def: a continuous pain that is not very strong
ex: I have an ache in my back.
The medicine took away the ache.

senses.def: to feel a continuous, dull pain
ex: My legs ached after the long walk.
His head ached all afternoon.

senses.def: something good that you have done successfully through hard work
ex: Finishing the marathon was a great achievement.
The school is proud of its students' achievements.

senses.def: a chemical that can burn things; many acids taste sour
ex: Lemon juice contains a weak acid.
The acid burned a hole in the cloth.

senses.def: to accept that something is true or exists
ex: He acknowledged that he had made a mistake.
The company acknowledges the problem.

senses.def: to show that you have received something or seen someone
ex: She acknowledged my email within an hour.
He acknowledged me with a nod.

senses.def: describing a musical instrument that makes sound without electrical equipment
ex: He played an acoustic guitar at the party.
They gave an acoustic concert in the park.

senses.def: relating to sound or hearing
ex: The hall has excellent acoustic qualities.

senses.def: a person you know a little but who is not a close friend
ex: She is just an acquaintance from work.
He has many acquaintances but few close friends.

senses.def: to get something, especially by buying it or by your own effort
ex: The museum acquired three new paintings.
He acquired a good knowledge of French.

senses.def: a unit for measuring land, equal to about 4,000 square metres
ex: The farm covers fifty acres.
They bought two acres of land near the lake.

senses.def: the size of an area of land, measured in acres
ex: The farmer increased his acreage of wheat this year.
The estate has a large acreage.

senses.def: involving difficult and skilful movements of the body, like those of an acrobat
ex: The goalkeeper made an acrobatic save.
The dancers performed an acrobatic routine.

senses.def: difficult physical movements such as jumping and balancing, done to entertain
ex: The children watched the acrobatics at the circus.
Her acrobatics on the bars amazed the crowd.

senses.def: from one side of something to the other
ex: The river is narrow, so we can swim across.
She walked across to say hello.

senses.def: from one side of something to the other side
ex: He ran across the road.
There is a bridge across the river.

senses.def: in all parts of a place or group
ex: The news spread across the country.

senses.def: a single thing that someone does
ex: It was an act of kindness.
He was arrested for a violent act.

senses.def: a law made by a government
ex: The new act protects workers' rights.

senses.def: one of the main parts of a play, opera or show
ex: The hero dies in the last act.

senses.def: to do something in order to deal with a situation
ex: We must act now before it is too late.
He acted quickly and called the police.

senses.def: to perform a part in a play or film
ex: She acts in a television series.

senses.def: always busy or full of energy; doing many things
ex: My grandfather is still very active.
She leads an active life.

senses.def: taking part in something and not only watching
ex: He is an active member of the club.

senses.def: in a way that involves real effort and attention
ex: The company is actively looking for new staff.
She actively takes part in class discussions.

senses.def: a woman whose job is acting in plays, films or television
ex: She wants to be a famous actress.
The actress won an award for her role.

senses.def: real, as opposed to what was thought or planned
ex: The actual cost was higher than we expected.
Nobody knows the actual reason for his leaving.

mistake.wrong: The actual situation is very bad now.
mistake.right: The current situation is very bad now.
mistake.note: actual is a false friend of Arabic حالي; use current or present to mean 'at this time'.

senses.def: used to say what is true or real, often when it is surprising
ex: I actually saw the president at the airport.
It was actually quite easy.

senses.def: used when you correct someone or add a different opinion politely
ex: Actually, I don't like coffee.

mistake.wrong: Actually, the weather is cold now.
mistake.right: Currently, the weather is cold.
mistake.note: actually does not mean 'at the present time'; Arabic حالياً is currently or at the moment.

senses.def: very serious or severe, and needing quick attention
ex: There is an acute shortage of water.
He was taken to hospital with acute pain.

senses.def: very sensitive and quick to notice things
ex: Dogs have an acute sense of smell.

senses.def: a picture, short film or notice that tries to sell something
ex: I saw an ad for a new phone.
They put an ad in the newspaper.

senses.def: to change your behaviour so that it suits a new situation
ex: It took her a while to adapt to life in London.
Animals must adapt to survive.

senses.def: to change something so that it is suitable for a new use
ex: The book was adapted for television.
We adapted the room to suit a baby.

mistake.wrong: He adapted with the new climate.
mistake.right: He adapted to the new climate.
mistake.note: Use adapt to, not adapt with.

senses.def: a person who cannot stop taking a harmful drug or doing something harmful
ex: He is a drug addict and needs help.
She is a social media addict.

senses.def: unable to stop taking a harmful drug or doing something harmful
ex: He became addicted to gambling.
Many teenagers are addicted to their phones.

mistake.wrong: He is addicted in smoking.
mistake.right: He is addicted to smoking.
mistake.note: Use addicted to, followed by a noun or -ing form.

senses.def: the state of being unable to stop taking a harmful drug or doing something harmful
ex: She is fighting an addiction to alcohol.
Drug addiction can ruin families.

senses.def: a substance added in small amounts to food or other products
ex: This juice contains no artificial additives.
Some additives keep food fresh for longer.

senses.def: produced by adding things together
ex: The effect is additive, so each dose increases the result.

senses.def: very good at doing something that needs skill
ex: She is adept at solving problems.
He became adept at using the new software.

senses.def: a person who is very good at something
ex: He is an adept in the art of negotiation.

senses.def: enough in quantity or good enough in quality for a particular purpose
ex: The room was small but adequate for one person.
We do not have adequate time to finish.

senses.def: to continue to follow a rule, belief or plan (adhere to)
ex: All staff must adhere to the safety rules.
She adheres to a strict diet.

senses.def: to stick firmly to a surface
ex: The tape adheres to most surfaces.

senses.def: next to or joined to something else
ex: We booked two adjoining rooms.
The garden has an adjoining field.

senses.def: a small change made to improve something or make it fit
ex: I made a few adjustments to the plan.
The seat needs a small adjustment.

senses.def: the process of getting used to a new situation
ex: Moving abroad requires a big adjustment.

senses.def: the activities involved in running a company, school or other organisation
ex: She works in hospital administration.
Too much administration takes time from teaching.

senses.def: a government, especially in the US, or the group of people who run an organisation
ex: The administration announced a new tax.

senses.def: relating to the work of running an organisation
ex: She has an administrative job at the university.
The office handles all administrative tasks.

senses.def: deserving respect and approval
ex: It was an admirable decision to help the poor.
She showed admirable courage.

senses.def: permission or the right to enter a place or join a school
ex: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.
She applied for admission to the university.

senses.def: a statement in which you agree that something bad is true
ex: His silence was an admission of guilt.

senses.def: to say that you did something bad or that something unpleasant is true
ex: He admitted that he broke the window.
She admitted her mistake.

senses.def: to allow someone to enter a place or join an organisation
ex: He was admitted to hospital with a broken leg.

senses.def: to legally take another person's child into your family and care for it
ex: They adopted a baby girl last year.
She wants to adopt a dog from the shelter.

senses.def: to begin to use a new idea, method or plan
ex: The school adopted a new way of teaching maths.
Many firms have adopted this technology.

senses.def: legally taken into a family as a son or daughter
ex: She is their adopted daughter.
He grew up in an adopted family.

senses.def: chosen as your own, especially a country or home
ex: She loves her adopted country.

senses.def: the legal process of taking another person's child into your family
ex: The couple are thinking about adoption.
Adoption can give a child a loving home.

senses.def: the decision to start using a new idea, method or plan
ex: The adoption of the new system saved money.

senses.def: very attractive in a way that makes you feel love
ex: Their baby is absolutely adorable.
What an adorable little puppy!

senses.def: to love someone or something very much
ex: She adores her grandchildren.
I adore chocolate cake.

senses.def: a chemical in the body that makes the heart beat faster when you are excited or afraid
ex: Adrenaline helped him to run faster.
Skiing gives me an adrenaline rush.

senses.def: fully grown or developed
ex: An adult elephant can weigh six tonnes.
She spent her adult life in Cairo.

senses.def: a person who is fully grown and legally responsible for their actions
ex: Tickets cost five pounds for adults.
Children must come with an adult.

senses.def: to move forward towards a place or goal
ex: The army advanced slowly across the valley.
Science has advanced a lot in fifty years.

senses.def: progress or an improvement in knowledge or skill
ex: Medical advances save millions of lives.
There have been great advances in technology.

senses.def: before something happens (in advance)
ex: Please book your tickets in advance.

senses.def: something good about a situation that helps you to succeed
ex: Speaking two languages is a big advantage.
Living near work has many advantages.

senses.def: to use a situation for your own benefit (take advantage of)
ex: Don't take advantage of her kindness.

senses.def: willing to try new, exciting or dangerous things
ex: She is adventurous and loves exploring new places.
Try something more adventurous on the menu.

senses.def: a person or team that you compete or fight against
ex: The two chess players were old adversaries.
He defeated his political adversary.

senses.def: an opinion that someone gives you about what you should do
ex: Can you give me some advice?
My teacher gave me a good piece of advice.

mistake.wrong: He gave me many advices. / I advice you to rest.
mistake.right: He gave me a lot of advice. / I advise you to rest.
mistake.note: advice (noun, /s/) is uncountable. advise (verb, /z/) is the action.

senses.def: giving advice and not having the power to make decisions
ex: He sits on an advisory committee.
She works for the school in an advisory role.

senses.def: to publicly support or recommend a particular idea, plan or way of doing something
ex: Many experts advocate earlier intervention.
Several studies advocate a four-day working week.
She advocates teaching coding in primary schools.

senses.def: a person who publicly supports an idea, plan or group
ex: He is a passionate advocate of free education.

mistake.wrong: Experts advocate for to start school later.
mistake.right: Experts advocate starting school later.
mistake.note: advocate + -ing or + noun. In British English, advocate for is less common; never add to.

senses.def: relating to beauty and the enjoyment of beautiful things
ex: The building has great aesthetic appeal.
They chose the colours for aesthetic reasons.

senses.def: an event or situation, especially an interesting or unpleasant one
ex: The whole affair was a surprise.
The wedding was a quiet family affair.

senses.def: matters that are important to a country or person (usually plural)
ex: He knows a lot about world affairs.
That is a private affair.

senses.def: a secret romantic relationship, especially with someone married
ex: The newspaper reported his affair.

senses.def: to have an influence on someone or something, causing a change
ex: The weather affects how I feel.
Pollution can affect your health.

mistake.wrong: The noise effected my sleep.
mistake.right: The noise affected my sleep.
mistake.note: affect is the verb meaning to influence; effect is usually a noun (a result).

senses.def: a gentle feeling of liking and caring for someone
ex: She has great affection for her grandmother.
The dog showed affection by licking my hand.

senses.def: showing that you love or like someone through your behaviour
ex: He is an affectionate father.
The cat is very affectionate.

senses.def: to have enough money to pay for something (usually with can)
senses.ar: يستطيع تحمّل ثمن؛ يقدر مادياً على
ex: We can't afford a new car.
Can you afford to take a holiday?

senses.def: to be able to do something without serious problems
ex: We cannot afford to wait any longer.

mistake.wrong: I can't afford to buy it because it is expensive for me.
mistake.right: I can't afford to buy it.
mistake.note: afford is normally used with can or could, and it already means that something costs too much.

senses.def: feeling fear because you think something bad may happen
ex: I'm afraid of spiders.
Don't be afraid; the dog is friendly.

senses.def: used to say politely that you are sorry about something
ex: I'm afraid I can't come tonight.

mistake.wrong: I am afraid from dogs.
mistake.right: I am afraid of dogs.
mistake.note: Use afraid of, not afraid from.

senses.def: at a later time than something else
ex: We eat dinner after the news.
I'll see you after lunch.

senses.def: following or behind someone or something
ex: The dog ran after the ball.

senses.def: at a later time
ex: They arrived at six, and we left soon after.

senses.def: at a time later than something else happened
ex: After she finished school, she travelled to Spain.
We went home after the film ended.

senses.def: at a later time, after something else has happened
ex: We had dinner and went for a walk afterwards.
Shortly afterwards, the phone rang.

senses.def: one more time; another time
ex: Please say that again.
I'm going to the beach again this summer.

senses.def: back to a previous place or state
ex: I felt well again after a few days.

senses.def: opposing or competing with someone or something
ex: Our team plays against the best club tomorrow.
Are you for or against the plan?

senses.def: touching or leaning on something
ex: She leaned her bike against the wall.

senses.def: not allowed by a rule or law
ex: Smoking here is against the law.

senses.def: a business that provides a particular service for other people
ex: She works for a travel agency.
The agency found him a flat.

senses.def: a government department that does a particular job
ex: A government agency checks food safety.

senses.def: a list of subjects to be talked about at a meeting
ex: The first item on the agenda is the budget.
Please send me the agenda before the meeting.

senses.def: a set of aims or plans that a person or group wants to achieve
ex: The new leader has a clear political agenda.

senses.def: a person whose job is to do business for another person or company
ex: She is a travel agent.
The actor's agent arranged the contract.

senses.def: a person who secretly collects information about another country
ex: The film is about a secret agent.

senses.def: angry and ready to attack or argue with other people
ex: The dog was aggressive towards strangers.
He becomes aggressive when he is tired.

senses.def: very determined and forceful in trying to succeed
ex: The company launched an aggressive advertising campaign.

senses.def: able to move quickly and easily
ex: The agile cat jumped onto the roof.
She is agile despite her age.

senses.def: able to think and understand quickly
ex: He has an agile mind.

senses.def: the ability to move quickly and easily, or to think quickly
ex: The gymnast showed great agility.
Mental agility helps in a fast-changing job.

senses.def: used after a period of time to show how long before now something happened
ex: I met him three years ago.
She left a few minutes ago.

mistake.wrong: I have seen him two days ago.
mistake.right: I saw him two days ago.
mistake.note: ago needs the past simple, not the present perfect.

senses.def: extreme physical or mental pain
ex: He was in agony after he broke his leg.
She waited in agony for the test results.

senses.def: pleasant and enjoyable
ex: We spent an agreeable afternoon in the garden.
He is an agreeable young man.

senses.def: willing to accept a plan or idea
ex: If you are agreeable, we will start tomorrow.

senses.def: [C] a decision or arrangement, often formal and written, between two or more groups
ex: The two sides finally reached an agreement.
They signed a trade agreement.

senses.def: [U] the situation in which people have the same opinion
ex: We're all in agreement on this point.

mistake.wrong: I am agree with you.
mistake.right: I agree with you.
mistake.note: agree is a verb. Do not add am / is / are before it.

senses.def: in front of someone or something, or further forward
ex: The road ahead is closed.
She walked ahead of the group.

senses.def: in the future, or before a planned time
ex: We need to plan ahead.
They booked the hotel ahead of time.

senses.def: help or support, especially money or food given to people in need
ex: The country sent aid after the floods.
She came to my aid at once.

senses.def: to help someone or something to do a job more easily
ex: New roads aid trade between the towns.
Good food aids recovery.
